Anchor.description:
A source anchor citing one registry source plus a locator inside it.

Anchors are first-class, structured fields — never free text. Per contract
§4, every clinical or scientific fact in a record carries one, and the
cited passage must actually support the claim it is attached to (checked
by the verification pipeline, #9).

locator.description:
Locator inside the source, written in the locator convention the
registry publishes for that source (chapter + section, or page where
the convention provides one — e.g. `ch34:cardiac-cycle` or `p.482`).
The string is intentionally untyped until #5 publishes per-source
locator conventions; this field exists so those conventions have
somewhere to land.

source_id.description:
Id of a source in the anchor source registry (#5). Only registry ids
may be cited; a fact whose only support is an unlisted source is
unanchored until that source is approved (contract §4).

AnchoredClaim.description:
A block of record text that is definitionally a clinical or scientific
claim — a rationale, an expected answer, or a teaching point — so at least
one source anchor is required (contract §4).

anchors.description:
Source anchors supporting the claim. At least one is required; the
cited passage must actually support it (checked by #9, not here).

AnchoredText.description:
A block of record text together with the source anchors supporting its
clinical and scientific claims (contract §4).

`anchors` may be empty only when the text asserts no clinical or
scientific fact — pure pedagogy (definitions, instructions to the
learner), or fictional-patient observations, which are invented and exempt
from anchoring. The JSON Schema cannot tell a claim from pedagogy; the
verification pipeline (#9) checks that every claim is anchored and that
each cited passage actually supports it.

anchors.description:
Source anchors for the claims this text makes. Empty only for pure
pedagogy or invented fictional-patient observations (contract §4).

Anchors for any clinical or scientific fact this option asserts that
the rationale's refutation does not address — contract §4 requires
such a fact to carry its own anchor (or the option to be rewritten).
Empty in the ordinary case.

label.description: Option label, `A`–`E`, unique within the record.

text.description:
Option text. A distractor is a wrong answer by design and is normally
anchored through the rationale's refutation (contract §4).

McqRationale.description:
The MCQ rationale — the issue requires explaining the key *and* why the
strongest distractor is wrong, so the two halves are separate fields.

key_explanation.description:
Why the keyed option is the best answer (mechanism, guideline
concordance, or classic teaching point — contract §5).

strongest_distractor.description:
Why the strongest distractor is wrong — a false claim, or a true
statement that is not the best answer in context. Its anchors support
the refutation, not the distractor's wording (contract §4).

Provenance.description:
How a record was produced — enough to reproduce or audit its drafting.

Model-drafted records carry `model` and `prompt_version`;
template-generated records carry `template_version`. Hand-written records
(fixtures, the gold seed set) name their author or checklist in
`generator`.

generator.description:
Identifier of the generator that produced the record — a procedural
template name, a teacher-model pipeline id, or a human author tag.

model.description: Teacher model identifier, when the record was model-drafted.

prompt_version.description: Version of the prompt used with the teacher model, when applicable.

template_version.description: Version of the procedural template, when template-generated.

RecordId.description: Unique record identifier: a lowercase slug of 3-64 characters.

RecordLabel.description:
A label in a record's metadata — exceptional conditions the contract
requires to be visible on the record itself.

This is a closed set: new labels are added here first, not written as
free-form strings.

oneOf.description:
The record is retained even though every one of its anchors cites a
superseded source — the only case where contract §7 lets such a
record stay in the dataset, and only when this label is present.

SchemaVersion.description: Version of the record schema this record conforms to.

SourceId.description: Id of a source in the anchor source registry: a lowercase slug of 3-64 characters. Registry ids are edition-scoped so the cited edition or year is visible (contract §7).

Subdomain.description:
`subdomain` — the twenty-five taxonomy subdomain slugs (taxonomy §3.2).

Every subdomain has exactly one parent domain; the mapping is enforced by
[`Subdomain::parent_domain`] and checked by each record's `validate`
method, since the domain/subdomain pairing cannot be expressed in JSON
Schema alone.

oneOf.description: Chemical & physical foundations of biological systems.
Structure and function of biological macromolecules.
Processes governing cellular organization and function.
Unique aspects of animal structure and function.
Translation of chemical and physical sciences.

Tier.description:
`tier` — difficulty tiers, defined per format (taxonomy §3.3–§4). The same
tier name means different things in an MCQ, a case vignette, and a tutoring
example; a record's tier is always interpreted relative to its format.

VerificationStatus.description:
Where a record sits on the path to the dataset (contract §8).

Exactly these four values. Only the verification & admission pipeline (#9)
may advance a record's status; generators always write `unverified`, and
nothing outside #9 writes `key-checked`, `anchor-checked`, or `admitted`.
This schema defines the enum — it does not perform the advancement.

oneOf.description: Drafted but not yet checked; never reaches the dataset.
Source anchors resolved and confirmed to support their claims (#9).

Passed verification and admitted into the dataset by the admission
gate (#9); counts toward coverage-matrix fill (taxonomy §5).

description:
A single-best-answer multiple-choice question (taxonomy §3.3 `mcq`,
tier definitions §4.1).

contract_version.description:
Version of `docs/contract.md` this record was admitted under (contract
§9). `null` until the admission gate (#9) sets it; required non-blank
once `verification_status` is `admitted` — enforced by
[`McqRecord::validate`].

key.description:
Label of the correct option. Must match one of `options[].label` —
enforced by [`McqRecord::validate`], beyond what JSON Schema expresses.

labels.description:
Record-level metadata labels; empty in the ordinary case. See
[`RecordLabel`] for the closed set — e.g. `historical_superseded`
marks a record retained on superseded sources (contract §7).

options.description: Answer options: 4–5, each with a unique `A`–`E` label.

rationale.description:
Why the key is the best answer and why the strongest distractor is
wrong. The refutation is anchored here; a fact another distractor
asserts that the refutation does not address carries its own anchor
on the option (contract §4).

stem.description:
The question stem. Factual claims in the stem carry anchors on this
field (contract §4).

subdomain.description:
Taxonomy subdomain; must belong to `domain` (taxonomy §3.2). Checked
by [`McqRecord::validate`] — JSON Schema cannot express the pairing.

taxonomy_version.description:
Version of `docs/taxonomy.md` this record was classified under
(taxonomy §6).

tier.description: Difficulty tier, interpreted per the `mcq` definitions (taxonomy §4.1).

verification_status.description: Verification status; advanced only by the pipeline in #9.
